card.name: Punctuation after warning statements
card.fires_on: Colons, periods and bullets that end a warning or precaution phrase in drug labels, often after 'WARNING' or after a safety instruction. Also a few linking words such as 'a' or 'These' in the same warning text.

modes.label: Colon after WARNING
modes.description: The colon right after the word WARNING in an overdose or keep-out-of-reach notice.
modes.example: In case of accidental overdose, call a doctor or poison control center immediately. WARNING<<:>> Folic acid alone is improper therapy in

modes.label: Period ending a patient instruction
modes.description: A sentence-ending period after a patient instruction or caution, just before the next instruction.
modes.example: Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do other dangerous activities until you know how tranylcypromine sulfate tablets affects you<<.>> Do not drink alcohol while taking trany

modes.label: Bullet or linking word
modes.description: A list bullet or short linking word that starts the next statement in a caution section.
modes.example: Stop use and ask<< a>> health care professional if symptoms persist for more

card.writes: It seems to suppress odd multilingual tokens and mildly promote words like 'certain', but the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It marks the end of a warning or caution phrase, where another safety statement is about to begin.
